Eate not with an enuious man, and desire not his meates. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Eate not with a niggard, lest he be secretly greued, outwardly dissembling, and thyself repent it.

verses.text: Because after the similitude of a southsayer, and diuiner, he esteemeth that which he knoweth not. Eate and drinke, wil he say to thee: and his minde is not with thee.
The meates which thou hadst eaten thou shalt vomite vp: and shalt lose thy beautiful wordes.
Speake not in the eares of the vnwise: because they wil despise the doctrine of thy speach. <na>[1]</na>
Touch not the boundes of litle ones: and into the filde of pupils enter not. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Hurt not orphanes: for they are deare to God.

verses.text: For their nerekinsman is strong: and he wil iudge their cause against thee.
Let thy hart enter into doctrin: and thyne eares to wordes of knowlege. <na>[1]</na>
Withdrawe not discipline from a childe: for if thou shalt strike him with the rod, he shal not die. <na>[1]</na>
Thou shalt strike him with the rod: and deliuer his soule from hel.
My sonne, if thy minde shal be wise, my hart shal be glad with thee: <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Vertues of children are ioyful to the parentes.

verses.text: And my reines shal reioyce, when thy lippes shal speake right thinges.
Let not thy hart enuie sinners: but in the feare of our Lord be thou al the day: <na>[1]</na>
because thou shalt haue hope in the later end, and thyn exaltation shal not be taken away. <na>[1]</na>
Heare my sonne, & be wise: & direct thy minde in the way. <na>[1]</na>
Be not in the feastes of great drinkers, nor in their comessations, which contribute flesh together to eate:
because they that are geuen to drinking, and that pay shottes, shal be consumed, and drousines shal be clothed with ragges. <na>[1]</na>
Heare thy father, that begot thee: and contemne not thy mother when she is old. <na>[1]</na>
Bye truth, and sel not wisedom, and doctrine, and intelligence. <na>[1]</na>
The father of the iust reioyceth with gladnes: he that hath begotten a wiseman, shal reioyce in him. <na>[1]</na>
Let thy father be glad, and thy mother, and let her reioyce that bare thee.
My sonne geue me thy hart: & let thyne eies kepe my wayes. <na>[1]</na>
For an harlot is a deepe dich: & a strange woman a narrow pitte.
She lyeth in wayt in the way as a robber, and whom she shal see not circumspect, she wil kil.
To whom is woe? to whose father woe? to whom browles? to whom diches? to whom woundes without cause? to whom bloud sheeding eies? <na>[1]</na>
Is it not to them that passe their time in wine, and studie to drinke out their cuppes?
Behold not wine when it waxeth yelow, when the colour therof shal shine in the glasse: it goeth in pleasantly, <na>[1]</na>
but in the end, it wil bite like a snake, and as a basiliske it wil powre abrode poysones. <na>[1]</na>
Thine eies shal see strange wemen, and thy hart shal speake peruerse thinges. <na>[1]</na>
And thou shalt be as one sleeping in the middes of the sea, and as the gouernour fast a sleepe, the sterne being lost. <na>[1]</na>
And thou shalt say: They haue beaten me, but I was not greeued: they drew me, and I felt not: When shal I awake, and finde wines againe? <na>[1]</na>
EMVLATE not euil men, neither desire thou to be with them: <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Flee euil companie, lest thou be alured to vice.

verses.text: because their mind doth meditate robberies, and their lippes speake deceites.
By wisedom the house shal be built, and by prudence it shal be strengthened. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: VVisdom and vertues, not wickednes, do prosper temporally and spiritualy.

verses.text: In doctrine the cellars shal be replenished with al precious, and most beautiful substance.
A wiseman is strong: and a lerned man, strong and valiant.
Because warre is managed by due ordering & there shal be saluation where manie counsels are. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Counsel in warres, and other great affayres.

verses.text: Wisedom is high for a foole, in the gate he shal not open his mouth.
He that thinketh to doe euils, shal be called a foole. <na>[1]</na>
The cogitation of a foole is sinne: and a detracter the abomination of men. <na>[1]</na>
If thou despaire being wearie in the day of distresse: thy strength shal be diminished. <na>[1]</na>
Deliuer them that are led to death: and those that are drawen to death cease not to deliuer. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: VVorkes of mercie, according to our habilitie.

verses.text: If thou say: I am not of force: he that seeth into the hart, he vnderstandeth, and nothing deceiueth the keeper of thy soule, and he shal render to a man according to his workes.
Eate honie my sonne, because it is good, and the honie-combe most sweete to thy throte: <na>[1]</na>
so also the doctrine of wisedom to thy soule: which when thou shalt finde, thou shalt haue hope in the later end, and thy hope shal not perish. <na>[1]</na>
Lie not in wayte, nor seeke impietie in the house of the iust, nor spoile his rest. <na>[1]</na>
For seuen <na>[1]</na> times shal the iust fal, and shal rise againe: but the impious shal fal into euil. <na>[2]</na>
When thine enemie shal fal, be not glad, and in his ruine let not thy hart reioyce: <na>[1]</na>
Lest perhaps our Lord see, and it displease him, and he take away his wrath from him.
Contend not with the most wicked, nor emulate the impious: <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Haue peace with al: so much as may be.

verses.text: because euil men haue not hope of thinges to come, and the lampe of the impious shal be extinguished.
Feare our Lord, my sonne, and the king: & with detracters medle not: <na>[1]</na>
because their perdition shal sodenly rise: and the ruine of both who knoweth?
These thinges also to the wise: to know a person in iudgement is not good. <na>[1]</na>
They that say to the impious: Thou art iust: peoples shal curse them, and tribes shal detest them. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Equitie in iudgement, condemning the guiltie, & deliuering the innocent, is very gratful to al.

verses.text: They that rebuke him, shal be praysed: and blessing shal come vpon them.
He shal kisse the lippes, who answereth right wordes.
Prepare thy worke abrode, and diligently til thy ground: that afterward thou mayst build thy house. <na>[1]</na>
Be not witnes without cause against thy neighbour: neither alure any man with thy lippes. <na>[1]</na>
Say not: As he hath done to me, so wil I doe to him: I wil render to euerie one according to his worke. <na>[1]</na>
I passed by the filde of a slothful man, and by the vineyard of a foolish man: <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Diligent labour, and vigilance to prouide necessaries, and to auoide beggerie.

verses.text: and behold nettels had filled it wholy, and thornes had couered the face therof, and the wal of stones was destroyed.
Which when I had seene, I layd it in my hart, and by the example I lerned discipline.
A litle I say, thou shalt sleepe, a litle thou shalt slumber, a litle shalt thou ioyne thy handes together, to rest:
and as a poste, pouertie shal come to thee, & beggerie as a man armed.
THese <na>[1]</na> also are the parables of Salomon, which the men of Ezechias king of Iuda wrote out.

notes.text: The 2. part. More Parables of Salomon written by others.

verses.text: It is the glorie of God to conceale the word, and the glorie of kinges to search the speach. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Gods workes are not al reueled.

verses.text: The heauen aboue, and the earth beneth, and the hart of kinges is vnscrutable. <na>[1]</na>
Take away the rust from siluer, and there shal comeforth a most pure vessel:
Take away impietie from the kings countenance, and his throne shal be established with iustice. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Publique iustice and punishment of sinne.

verses.text: Appeare not glorious before the king, and in the place of great men stand not. <na>[1]</na>
For it is better that it be said to thee: Come vp hither; then that thou be humbled before the prince. <na>[1]</na>
The thinges which thy eies haue sene, vtter not quickly in a brawle: lest afterward thou canst not amend it, when thou hast dishonoured thy frend. <na>[1]</na>
Treate thy cause with thy frend, and reueale not a secret to a stranger: <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Compose controuersies secretly, rather then contend in publique court.

verses.text: lest perhaps he insult against thee, when he heareth, and cease not to vpbraide thee. Grace and frendshipe deliuer: <na>[1]</na> which kepe to thyself, lest thou become reprochful.
Apples of gold in siluer beddes, he that speaketh a word in his time. <na>[1]</na>
A golden earlet, and a shining precious stone, he that rebuketh a wiseman, and an obedient eare. <na>[1]</na>
As the cold of snow in the day of haruest, so a faithful legate to him, that sent him, maketh his soule to rest. <na>[1]</na>
Cloudes, and winde, and no rayne folowing, a glorious man, and not accomplishing his promises. <na>[1]</na>
By patience the prince shal be pacified, and a soft tongue shal breake hardnes. <na>[1]</na>
Thou hast found honie, eate that which sufficeth thee, lest perhaps being filled thou vomite it vp. <na>[1]</na>
Withdraw thy foote from the house of thy neighbour, lest some time hauing his fil he hate thee. <na>[1]</na>
A dart, and sword, and a sharpe arrow, a man that speaketh false testimonie against his neighbour. <na>[1]</na>
A rotten tooth, and wearie foote, he that hopeth vpon the vnfaithful in the day of distresse, <na>[1]</na>

and that loseth his cloke in the day of cold. Vineger in <na>[1]</na> nither, he that singeth songes to a naughtie hart. <na>[2]</na> As a moth the garment, and a worme the woode: so the sadnes of a man hurteth the hart. <na>[3]</na>
If thine enemie shal hunger, geue him meate: if he thirst, geue him water to drinke: <na>[1]</na>
for thou shalt heape hote coales vpon his head, and our Lord wil reward thee. <cr>[1]</cr>
The northwinde dissipateth raynes, & a sad looke the tongue that detracteth. <na>[1]</na>
It is better to sitte in a corner of the house toppe, then with a brawling woman, and in a common house. <na>[1]</na>
Cold water to a thirstie soule, and good tydings from a far countrie. <na>[1]</na>
A fountaine trubled with the foote, and a vaine corrupted, the iust falling before the impious. <na>[1]</na>
As he that eateth much honie, it is not good for him: so he that is a searcher of the maiestie, shal be oppressed of the glorie. <na>[1]</na>
As a citie being open and without compasse of walles, so a man that can not represse his spirit in speaking. <na>[1]</na>
AS snow in the summer, and rayne in the haruest: so is glorie vndecent for a foole. <na>[1]</na>
As a birde flying to other places, & a sparow going whither he list: so a curse vttered in vaine shal light vpon some man. <na>[1]</na>
A whippe for a horse, and a snaffle for an asse, and a rod on the back of the vnwise. <na>[1]</na>
Answer not a foole according to his follie, lest thou be made like to him. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Answer a foole wisely: detecting his follie.

verses.text: Answer a foole according to his follie, lest he seme to himself to be wise.
Lame of feete, and drinking iniquitie, he that sendeth wordes by a foolish messenger. <na>[1]</na>
As a lame man hath fayre legges in vaine: so a parable is vndecent in the mouth of fooles. <na>[1]</na>
As he that casteth a stone into the heape of Mercurie: so he that geueth honour to the vnwise. <na>[1]</na>
As if a thorne should grow in the hand of the drunkard: so a parable in the mouth of fooles. <na>[1]</na>
Iudgement determineth causes: and he that putteth a foole to silence, apeaseth angers. <na>[1]</na>
As a dog that returneth to his vomite, so the vnwise that reiterateth his follie. <na>[1]</na>
Hast thou sene a man seeme to himselfe wise? the foole shal haue hope rather then he. <na>[1]</na>
The slothful sayth: A lyon is in the way, and a lyonesse in the iourneis: <na>[1]</na>
as a doore turneth on his hinge so the slothful in his bed. <na>[1]</na>
The slothful hideth his hand vnder the armehole, and is greeued if he turneth it to his mouth. <na>[1]</na>
The slothful seemeth wiser to himselfe, then seuen men speaking sentences. <na>[1]</na>
As he that taketh a dog by the eares, so he that passeth by impatient, and medleth with an other mans brawle. <na>[1]</na>
As he is hurtful that shooteth arrowes, and speares vnto death:
so a man, that hurteth his frende fraudulently: and when he is taken with al sayth: I did it in iest. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Vnfained frendship, especially in familiar acquaintance.

verses.text: When wood fayleth, the fire shal be extinguished: and the whisperer taken away, brawles cease. <na>[1]</na>
As coles to burning coles, and wood to fire, so an angrie man rayseth brawles. <na>[1]</na>
The wordes of the whisperer as it were simple, and the same come to the inmost partes of the bellie. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Heare not whisperers of euil reportes.

verses.text: As if thou wouldest adorne an earthen vessel with drossie siluer, so swelling lippes ioyned with a most wicked hart. <na>[1]</na>
An enemie is perceiued by his lippes, when he shal handle deceites in his hart. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: VVhose flaterie and soft speach are suspicious, they wil fal at last into their owne trappes, truth preuailing.

verses.text: When he shal submit his voyce, beleue him not: because there are seuen mischiefes in his hart.
He that couereth hatred fraudulently, his malice shal be reuealed in the councel.
He that diggeth a pit, shal fal into it: and he that rolleth a stone, it shal returne to him.
A deceitful tongue loueth not truth, and a slipper mouth worketh ruines.
BOast not for to morow, being ignorant what the day to come may bringforth. <na>[1]</na>
Let an other prayse thee, and not thine owne mouth: a stranger and not thine owne lippes. <na>[1]</na>
A stone is heauie, and sand weightie: but the anger of a foole is heauier then both. <na>[1]</na>
Anger hath no mercie, nor furie breaking forth: and the violence of a moued spirit who can susteyne? <na>[1]</na>
Better is manifest correption, then loue hidden. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Love friendly severity, not enemy's flattery.

verses.text: Better are the woundes of him that loueth, then the fraudulent kisses of him that hateth.
A soule that is ful shal treade vpon the honiecombe: and a soule that is hungrie shal take bitter also for sweete. <na>[1]</na>
As a bird fleeting from her nest, so a man that forsaketh his place. <na>[1]</na>
The hart is delighted with oyntement and diuers odours: and with the good counsels of a frend the soule is sweetned. <na>[1]</na>
Thy frend, and thy fathers frend do not leaue: and goe not into thy brothers house in the day of thyne affliction. Better is a neighbour neere thene a brother far of. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Old freindes are better, & surer then a kinsman.

verses.text: Studie wisedom my sonne, & make my hart ioyful, that thou maist make answer to the vpbrayder. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Be wise euen for thy fathers sake.

verses.text: . The subtel man seeing euil, hideth himself: litle ones passing through haue susteyned euil detriments.
Take his garment, that hath bene suretie for a stranger: and for alienes take from him a pledge. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Foresee and preuent dangers. Trust not enimies.

verses.text: He that blesseth his neighbour with a loud voice, rising in the night, he shal be like him that curseth. <na>[1]</na>
Dropping through in the day of cold, and a brawling woman are compared together: <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Tolerate incorrigible brawlers with patience; lest they become worse, by thy striuing to amend them.

verses.text: He that reteyneth her, as he that should hold the winde, and shal cal in the oyle of his right hand.
Iron is sharpened with iron, and a man sharpeneth the face of his frend.
He that kepeth the feegtree, shal eate the frute therof: and he that is the keper of his master, shal be glorified. <na>[1]</na>
As in waters the countenance of them that looke therin shyneth, so the hartes of men are manifest to the prudent. <na>[1]</na>
Hel and perdition are neuer filled: in like maner also the eies of men are vnsatiable. <na>[1]</na>

As siluer is tried in the forge, and gold in the fornace: so a man is proued by the mouth of him that praiseth. <na>[1]</na> The hart of the wicked seeketh after euils, but the righteous hart seeketh after knowlege. <na>[2]</na>
If thou shalt bray a foole in a morter, as when a pestle striketh vpon ptisane, his follie shal not be taken from him. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Striue not to teach a foole.

verses.text: Know diligently the countenance of thy cattel, and consider thy flockes: <na>[1]</na>
For thou shalt not haue power alwayes: but a crowne shal be geuen into generation and generation. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: VVhiles thou art in this life.

verses.text: The medowes are open, and the grene herbes haue appeared, and the grasse is gathered out of the mountaines.
Lambes for thy garment: and kiddes the price of the filde.
Let the milke of the goates suffice thee for thy meates, and for the necessities of thy house: and for victual to thy handmaides. <cr>[1]</cr><na>[2]</na>

notes.text: Be content with things necessary, and they shall be given to thee.

verses.text: THE impious fleeth, no man pursewing: but the iust confident as a lyon, shal be without terrour. <na>[1]</na>
For the sinnes of the land the princes therof shal be manie: & for the wisedom of a man, & the knowlege of those thinges that are said, the life of the prince shal be longer. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: General pietie of the people procureth Gods fauour.

verses.text: A poore man calumniating the poore, is like a vehement showre, wherby famine is gotten. <na>[1]</na>
They that forsake the lawe, praise the impious: they that kepe it, are set on fire against him. <na>[1]</na>
Euil men thinke not on iudgement: but they that seeke after our Lord, marke al thinges. <na>[1]</na>
Better is a poore man walking in his simplicitie, then the rich in crooked wayes. <na>[1]</na>
He that kepeth the law is a wise sonne, but he that feedeth gluttons, shameth his father. <na>[1]</na>
He that heapeth together riches by vsuries and ocker, gathereth them for him that is liberal to the poore. <na>[1]</na>
He that turneth away his eares from hearing the law, his prayer shal be execrable. <na>[1]</na>
He that deceiueth the iust in a wicked way, shal fal into his destruction: and the simple shal possesse his goodes. <na>[1]</na>
The rich man seemeth to him self wise: but the poore man being prudent shal searche him. <na>[1]</na>
In the exultation of the iust there is much glorie: when the impious reigne ruines of men. <na>[1]</na>
He that hideth his wicked deedes, shal not be directed: but he that shal confesse, and shal forsake them, shal obtayne mercie. <na>[1]</na>
Blessed is the man, that is alwayes fearful: but he that is of an obstinate mynde, shal fal into euil. <na>[1]</na>
A roaring lyon, and hungrie beare, an impious prince ouer the poore people. <na>[1]</na>
A prince lacking prudence, shal oppresse many by calumnie: but he that hateth auarice, his dayes shal be made long. <na>[1]</na>
A man that doth calumniat the bloud of a soule, if he shal flee into a lake, no man abideth. <na>[1]</na>
He that walketh simply shal be saued: he that goeth peruerse wayes, shal fal once. <na>[1]</na>
He that tilleth his ground, shal be filled with breads: but he that purseweth idlnesse, shal be replenished with pouertie. <na>[1]</na>
A faithful man shal be much praysed: but he that hasteneth to be rich, shal not be innocent. <na>[1]</na>
He that knoweth a person in iudgement, doth not wel: this man euen for a morsel of bread forsaketh the truth. <na>[1]</na>
A man, that hasteneth to be rich, and enuyeth others, is ignorant that pouertie shal come vpon him. <na>[1]</na>
He that rebuketh a man, shal afterward find fauour with him more then he, that by flatteries of tongue deceiueth. <na>[1]</na>
He that pilfereth any thing from his father, and from his mother: & saith this is no sinne, is the partaker of a mankiller. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: To robbe parents is a greuous crime.

verses.text: He that exulteth, and dilateth himselfe, rayseth brawles: but he that trusteth in our Lord, shal be healed. <na>[1]</na>
He that hath confidence in his owne hart, is a foole: but who so walketh wisely shal be saued. <na>[1]</na>
He that geueth to the poore, shal not lacke: he that despiseth him that asketh, shal susteyne penurie. <na>[1]</na>
When the impious shal rise, men shal be hid: when they shal perish, the iust shal be multiplied. <na>[1]</na>
THE man, that with stiffe necke contemneth him that rebuketh, soden destruction shal come vpon him: and health shal not folow him. <na>[1]</na>
In the multiplication of iust men, the common people shal reioyce: when the impious shal take princedom, the people shal mourne. <na>[1]</na>
A man that loueth wisedom, maketh his father glad: but he that maintaineth harlots, shal destroy his substance. <na>[1]</na>
A iust king setteth vp the land, a couetous man shal destroy it. <na>[1]</na>
A man, that with fayre, and fayned wordes speaketh to his frend, spreadeth a nette to his steppes. <na>[1]</na>
A snare shal intangle the wicked man sinning: and the iust shal praise and reioyce. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Iust ioy of the wickeds fal.

verses.text: The iust knoweth the cause of the poore: the impious is ignorant of knowlege. <na>[1]</na>
Pestilent men dissipate a citie: but the wise turne away furie. <na>[1]</na>
A wise man, if he contend with a foole, whether he be angrie, or whether he laugh, shal not finde rest. <na>[1]</na>
Men of bloud hate the simple: but iust men seeke his soule. <na>[1]</na>
A foole vttereth al his spirit: a wiseman differreth, and reserueth til afterward. <na>[1]</na>
A prince that gladly heareth wordes of lying, hath al his seruants impious. <na>[1]</na>
The pooreman and the creditour haue mette one an other: our Lord is illuminatour of both. <na>[1]</na>
The king, that iudgeth the poore in truth, his throne shal be replenished for euer. <na>[1]</na>
Rod and rebuke geueth wisedom: but the childe, that is left to his owne wil, confoundeth his mother. <na>[1]</na>
In the multiplication of the impious, wickednes shal be multiplied, and the iust shal see the ruines of them. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: God neuer permitteth al to be euil.

verses.text: Nurter thy sonne, and he shal refresh thee, and shal geue delightes to thy soule. <na>[1]</na>
When prophecie shal fayle, the people shal be dissipated: but he that keepeth the Law, is blessed. <na>[1]</na>
A seruant can not be taught by wordes: because he vnderstandeth that which thou sayst, and contemneth to answer. <na>[1]</na>
Hast thou seene a man swifte to speake? follie is rather to be hoped, then his amendement. <na>[1]</na>
He that nourisheth his seruant delicatly from his childhood, afterward shal feele him stubburne. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Subdue the flesh to the spirite.

verses.text: An angrie man prouoketh brawles: and he that is easie to indignation, shal be more prone to sinne. <na>[1]</na>
Humiliation foloweth the proude: and glorie shal receiue the humble of spirite. <na>[1]</na>
He that is partaker with a theefe, hateth his owne soule: he heareth one adiuring, and telleth not. <na>[1]</na>
He that feareth man, shal soone fal: he that trusteth in our Lord shal be lifted vp. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: Fear not men in God's cause,

verses.text: Manie seeke after the face of the prince: & the iudgement of euerie one commeth forth from our Lord. <na>[1]</na>

notes.text: remembering that God is Judge of all.

verses.text: The iust abhorre an impious man: & the impious abhorre them that are in the right way. <na>[1]</na> The sonne that keepeth the word, shal be out of perdition. <na>[2]</na>
THE wordes of the Gatherer the sonne of Vomiter. The vision, that the man spake, with whom God is, and who being strengthened by God abiding with him, sayd:
I am <na>(a)</na> most foolish of men, & the wisedom of men is not with me.

notes.label: a
notes.text: The wisest man best knoweth that he wanteth much of perfect wisdom yet in his humilitie supposeth, that others haue attained some what more then himself.

verses.text: I haue not learned wisedom, and haue not knowen the science of saints.

<na>(b)</na> Who hath ascended into heauen and descended? who hath conteyned the spirit in his handes? who hath bound the waters together as in a garment? who hath raysed vp al the borders of the earth? what is his name, and what is the name of his sonne, if thou know?

notes.label: b
notes.text: Christ the Sonne of God is wisdom it self, and as the Sonne of man hath perfect wisdom.

verses.text: Euerie word of God tryed by fyre, is a buckler to them that hope in him:
Adde not any thing to his wordes, and so thou be reproued and found a lyer:
Two thinges I haue asked thee, denie them not to me before I dye.
Vanitie, and lying wordes make far from me. Beggerie, and riches geue me not: geue only things necessarie for my sustenance:
lest perhaps being filled I be allured to denie, and may say: Who is the Lord? or being compelled by pouertie I may steale, and forsweare the name of my God.
<na>(c)</na> Accuse not a seruant to his master, lest perhaps he curse thee, and thou fal.

notes.label: c
notes.text: Bondslaues are to be pitied, and not affliction added to the afflicted.

verses.text: There is <na>(d)</na> a generation that curseth their father, and that blesseth not their mother.

notes.label: d
notes.text: Foure execrable vices. Ingratitude. Hypocrisie: Insolencie: Oppression of the poore.

verses.text: A generation, that semeth to it self cleane, & yet is not washed from their filthines.
A generation, whose eies are loftie, and the eielids therof set vp on high.
A generation, that for teeth hath swordes, and chaweth with theyr grinding teeth, that they may eate the needie out of the earth, and the poore from among men.
The horseleach hath <na>(e)</na> two daughters that say: Bring, bring. Three things are vnsatiable, the fourth neuer sayth it sufficeth.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Concupiscence of the flesh, & of the eyes. · Enuie, Luxurie, Auarice, & Ambition.

verses.text: Hel, and the mouth of the matrice, & the earth which is not satisfied with water: but the fyre neuer sayth it sufficeth.
The eie, that <na>(f)</na> scorneth his father, & that despiseth the trauail of his mother, in bearing him, let the rauens of the torrents pick it out, and the young of the eagle eate it.

notes.label: f
notes.text: Dishonour of parents shal be seuerely punished.

verses.text: Three thinges are hard to me, and of the fourth I am vtterly ignorant.
The way of an eagle in the ayre, the way of a serpent vpon a rocke, the way of a shippe in the middes of the sea, and <na>(g)</na> the way of a man in youth.

notes.label: g
notes.text: Yong men folowing carnal appetite, can no more geue account of their actions, then of the vvayes vvhich an eagle, a serpent, and a shippe haue passed.

verses.text: Such is also the way of an adulterous woman, which eateth, and wyping her mouth sayth: I haue done no euil.
By three thinges the earth is moued, and the fourth it can not susteyne.
By a seruant when he shal reigne: by a foole when he shal be filled with meate:
by an odious woman when she shal be taken in matrimonie: & by a bondwoman when she shal be heyre to her mistresse.
There are <na>(h)</na> foure the least thinges of the earth, and they are wiser then the wise.

notes.label: h
notes.text: By these examples are commended foure vertues, Industrie, Prudence, Concord, and Humilitie.

verses.text: The antes, a weake people, which prepareth in the haruest meate for themselues:
The leueret, a people not strong, which placeth his bed in the rocke:
The locust hath no king, and they go out al by their troopes:
The stellion stayeth on his handes, & tarieth in kings houses.
<na>(i)</na> There are three thinges which go wel, and the fourth that goeth happely.

notes.label: i
notes.text: Other foure Fortitude, Chastitie, Order, and Iustice.

verses.text: The lyon, the strongest of beastes shal feare at the meeting of none:
the cocke gyrded about the loines, and the ramme: also the king, against whom none can resist.
There is that <na>(k)</na> hath appeared a foole after that he was lifted vp on high: for if he had vnderstood, he would haue layd his hand vpon his mouth.

And he that <na>(l)</na> strongly presseth the pappes to wring out milke, strayneth out butter, and he that violently cleanceth his nose, wringeth out bloud: & he that prouoketh angers, bringeth forth discordes.

notes.label: l
notes.text: Moderation is necessarie in al actions.

chapters.summary: A right wiseman thinketh humbly of himself. 4. knowing that Gods workes are inscrutable, and perfect: 8. desireth truth in al thinges, & mediocritie in riches. 11. Abhorreth certaine sortes of men, 15. & certaine execrable thinges 18. noteth certaine things hard to be knowen: 21. other thinges intolerable: 24. others admirable. 32. the tongue dangerous. <na>[1]</na>

summary_notes.text: The fourth part. Other singular precepts, with praise of a prudent woman.

verses.text: THE <na>(a)</na> wordes of Lamuel the king. The vision wherwith his mother instructed him.

notes.label: a
notes.text: VVordes perteining to Salomon, spoken to him by his mother: who here calleth him Lamuel, signifying, God with him.

verses.text: What ô my beloued, what ô the beloued of my wombe, what ô beloued of my vowes?
Geue not thy substance to wemen, & thy riches to destroy kinges.
Geue not to kinges, ô Lamuel, geue not wine to kinges: because there is no secrete where drunknes reigneth,
& lest perhaps they drinke, & forget iudgements, & change the cause of the children of the poore.
Geue strong drinke to them that be sad, and wine vnto them, that are of a pensiue minde:
let them drinke, and forget their pouertie, and not remember their sorow any more.
Open thy mouth to <na>(b)</na> the dumme, & to the cause of al the children that passe:

notes.label: b
notes.text: Doctrine is most profitable to those, that are modestly dumme, more vvilling to heare then to speake.

verses.text: open thy mouth, <na>(c)</na> decree that which is iust, & iudge the needie & poore.

notes.label: c
notes.text: The chief & most proper office of a king is to do iustice.

verses.text: A valiant woman <na>(d)</na> who shal finde? far, and from the vtmost borders is the price of her.

notes.label: d
notes.text: A vvoman of such perfectió as is here described, is in dede rare, yet possible to be found.

verses.text: The hart of her husband trusteth in her, and he shal not neede spoyles.
She shal render good, and not euil, al the dayes of her life.
She hath sought wool and flaxe, and hath wrought by the counsel of her handes.
She is become as a marchants shippe, bringing her bread from farre.
And she hath risen in the night, and geuen pray to her houshold, and meates to her handmaides.
She hath vewed a filde, and bought it, of the fruite of her handes she hath planted a vineyard.
She hath gyrded her loines with strength, and hath strengthened her arme.
She hath tasted, and sene that her traficke is good: her lampe shal not be extinguished in the night.
She hath put her hand to strong thinges, and her fingers haue taken hold of <na>(e)</na> the spindle.

notes.label: e
notes.text: Flaxe on the distaffe signifieth purpose to do good workes, yarne on the spindle the vvorke vvel begune, which geueth confidence in God that the same shal be perfect and haue due revvard.

verses.text: She hath opened her hand to the needie, and stretched out her palmes to the poore.
She shal not feare for her house in the coldes of snow: for al her houshould are clothed with duble.
Tapestrie clothing she hath made to herself: silke, and purple is her garment.
Her husband is noble in the gates, when he shal sitte with the senatours of the land.
She <na>(f)</na> made sindon, and sold it, and deliuered a girdle to the Chananeite.

notes.label: f
notes.text: They make and sel cloth, which lerning and obseruing Gods lavv, do teach it others.

verses.text: Strength and beautie is her garment, and she shal laugh in the later day.
She hath opened her mouth to wisedom, and the law of clemencie is in her tongue.
She hath considered the pathes of her house, and hath not eaten her bread idle.
Her children arose, and commended her to be most blessed: her husband, and he praysed her.
Manie daughters haue gathered together riches: thou hast passed them al.
<na>(g)</na> Grace is deceitful, and beautie is vayne: the woman that feareth our Lord shal be praysed.

notes.label: g
notes.text: External comelines is not durable: but the feare of God is more vvorthie of praise.

verses.text: Geue ye to her <na>(h)</na> of the fruite of her handes: and let her workes praise her <na>(i)</na> in the gates.

notes.label: i
notes.text: at the tribunal seate of iudgement.

chapters.summary: An exhortation to chastitie, temperance, 8. and to workes of mercie. 10. with praise of a valiant wise woman.
